children: Fiona, the beloved Nile hippopotamus who captivated the internet in the late 2010s, died on Thursday after eating a hat that fell into her enclosure last week.
"We are in shock at the moment," Dave Jenike, director of the Cincinnati Zoo & Botanical Garden, said in a statement. "We did not expect this outcome. She fought until she couldn't anymore."

Fiona was born six weeks early in 2017, weighing only 29 pounds and requiring immediate critical care. Zookeepers shared near-constant updates about her progress, marking her journey from a baby hippopotamus to a 9-year-old that weighed more than 2,000 pounds. Her journey captured the hearts of viewers around the globe, inspiring children's books, an ice cream flavor, and even a training device for the Cincinnati Reds.

Zoo officials characterized the hat entering the enclosure as an accident. Fiona was originally asymptomatic, officials said, but her appetite soon started to decline. Veterinary staff tried for days to help move the hat out of her system, including via ultrasound, colonoscopy, and a vibration plate borrowed from a horse farm.

"Fiona captured the hearts of millions and became one of Cincinnati's most beloved icons," Amy Acton, the governor-elect of Ohio, said on social media. "Her story brought joy, hope, and a little extra magic to our state."

This isn't the first time the zoo has lost one of its fan-favorite animals. Harambe, a 17-year-old silverback gorilla, was put down in 2016 after a child climbed through a public barrier and dropped into his exhibit's moat. The decision to kill the gorilla, which zoo officials said was necessary to save the life of the child, drew public outrage and criticism from animal-rights groups.
